recap_lines: MCP drives a live Blender, and a bpy script runs it headless.
Add the python exit code flag, or a broken script exits zero.
Blender is Z-up, and the plus Y Up option puts its Z on Godot's Y.
Apply transforms, so the scale lives in the mesh and not on the node.

bookends.command: Quiz me on moving a model from Blender into Godot, with short game-making cases, one at a time. Use the terms unit scale, up axis, apply transforms, node scale, GLB, name suffix, collision shape, convex, triangle count and claim versus measurement. For each case I must name the exact term and say why its look-alike is wrong. Hold back the answer until I reply, then tell me if I was right.

beats.narration_text: Three boxes, a coding agent, an MCP server, and Blender with an add-on. MCP is a standard way for an AI app to call tools inside another program. The agent sends a request, and Blender runs it and sends back a result. Both sides follow one agreed set of message rules. Unlike the script route, MCP works on a live Blender window. For example, an agent asks a running Blender for the size of a crate you just modelled, and gets the numbers back.

For example, before an agent shapes rocks for your level in Blender, you enable the add-on inside Blender, start it, and register the server with your coding agent.

beats.narration_text: Headless Blender means running Blender with no window, from the command line. It is also called background mode. The b flag runs it in the background, the factory startup flag skips your own startup file, and the python flag runs the script. Nobody has to watch a screen. For example, after you change one measurement in your build script, an agent runs Blender headless to rebuild every fence prop in the level, then reads the printed sizes.

beats.narration_text: A ruler in metres, with the robot capsule and the post beside it. A unit is the length one coordinate step stands for, usually a metre. beats.narration_text: Unit scale is the factor that turns Blender units into metres. A mesh one point eight units tall is one point eight metres at unit scale one point zero, but one point eight centimetres at zero point zero one. A unit is the length of a step, and unit scale is the multiplier on it. For example, a sword built in a scene with the wrong unit scale arrives in the player's hand far too small to see.

beats.narration_text: Two sets of axes, Blender on the left and Godot on the right. The up axis is the axis that points up. Blender is Z-up, and glTF and Godot are Y-up. Godot's forward direction is minus Z. Both systems are right-handed. For example, in Godot a script that lifts a moving platform toward the ceiling raises the platform's Y position, not its Z, because Y is the up axis there.

beats.narration_text: Axis conversion is the step that turns one up axis into the other. The exporter's plus Y Up option rotates the model a quarter turn about X, the matrix shown, so Blender's Z extent becomes Godot's Y. The column's box was zero point two, zero point two, one point eight in Blender, and in Godot the one point eight sits on Y.
